questions.question: Sector AOB of a circle with centre O and radius r cm has angle AOB = 1.25 radians and area 15 cm^2. Find the exact value of r.
steps: Area of a sector = (1/2) r^2 theta.

questions.question: For the same sector (angle 1.25 radians, area 15 cm^2, radius r cm), find the exact length of the perimeter of the sector in simplest form.
steps: Perimeter = 2r + r theta (two radii plus the arc).

questions.question: A ceiling fan face consists of three identical sections congruent to OABCDO. OABO is a sector of radius 9 cm, OBCDO is a sector of radius 84 cm, and angle AOD = 2pi/3 radians. Given that arc AB is 15 cm, show that arc CD is 35.9 cm to 1 d.p.
steps: Angle AOB = arc AB / radius = 15/9 = 5/3 radians.
Angle COD = AOD - AOB = 2pi/3 - 5/3 = (2pi - 5)/3, about 0.4277 radians.
Arc CD = 84 x 0.4277 = 35.93 cm, so 35.9 cm to 1 d.p.

questions.question: The face of the fan is modelled as a flat surface made of the three identical sections. Find the perimeter of the face of the fan to the nearest cm.
steps: Outer boundary of one section: arc AB (15 cm), radial edge BC (84 - 9 = 75 cm), arc CD (35.93 cm), and the exposed part of radial edge DO beyond the 9 cm mark (84 - 9 = 75 cm).
Three sections: 3 x 200.93 = 602.8 cm, so 603 cm to the nearest cm.

questions.question: Treating the face of the fan as a flat surface made of three identical sections, find the surface area of the face of the fan to 3 significant figures, with units.
steps: Three sections: 3 x 1576.5 = 4729.6 cm^2, so 4730 cm^2 (3 s.f.).

questions.question: A badge is made of two congruent triangles AOC and BOC joined to sector AOB of a circle with centre O. AO = OB = 3 cm, OC = 5 cm, angle AOB = alpha, and the area of sector AOB is 7.2 cm^2. Show that alpha = 1.6 radians.

For the badge (AO = OB = 3 cm, OC = 5 cm, alpha = 1.6 radians, triangles AOC and BOC congruent), find (i) the area of the badge in cm^2 to 2 significant figures, and (ii) the perimeter of the badge in cm to 1 decimal place.
steps: Angle AOC = pi - alpha/2 = pi - 0.8, so sin(AOC) = sin(0.8) = 0.7174.
Area of triangle AOC = (1/2)(3)(5) sin(0.8) = 5.380 cm^2; two triangles give 10.76 cm^2.
(i) Badge area = sector 7.2 + 10.76 = 17.96 cm^2, so 18 cm^2 to 2 s.f.
Cosine rule in triangle AOC: AC^2 = 9 + 25 - 30 cos(pi - 0.8) = 34 + 30 cos(0.8) = 54.90, so AC = 7.409 cm.

questions.question: Triangle XYZ has XY = 6 cm, YZ = 9 cm, ZX = 4 cm and angle ZXY = alpha. Show that alpha = 2.22 radians to 3 significant figures.
steps: Cosine rule: YZ^2 = XY^2 + XZ^2 - 2(XY)(XZ) cos(alpha).
alpha = arccos(-0.6042) = 2.2195 radians, so 2.22 to 3 s.f.

questions.question: Point W lies on line XY and arc ZW is a major arc of the circle with centre X and radius 4 cm. Find the area, in cm^2, of the major sector XZWX.
steps: W lies on the circle, so XW = 4 cm.
Angle ZXW = alpha, so the major sector angle is 2pi - alpha = 4.0637 radians.

questions.question: The shaded region in Figure 4 is used as a logo. It is the major sector XZWX together with triangle XYZ. Calculate the area of the logo in cm^2.
Calculate the perimeter of the logo in Figure 4, in cm.
steps: Boundary of the logo = major arc ZW + ZY + YW.
ZY = 9 cm; YW = XY - XW = 6 - 4 = 2 cm.

questions.question: Figure 1 shows the plan of a stage: sector OBC of a circle with centre O, joined to two congruent triangles OAB and ODC, with AOD a straight line of length 12.5 m. Angle BOC = 2.4 radians and the area of sector OBC is 40 m^2. Find the radius of the sector, in m, to 2 decimal places.
Find the size of angle AOB, in radians, to 2 decimal places.
steps: A, O and D lie on a straight line, so AOB + BOC + COD = pi.
The triangles are congruent with O the midpoint of AD, so AOB = COD.

questions.question: Hence find the total area of the stage in m^2 to 1 decimal place.
steps: Each triangle OAB: OA = 12.5/2 = 6.25 m, OB = 5.7735 m, angle AOB = 0.3708 radians.

questions.question: Hence find the total perimeter of the stage in m to 1 decimal place.
steps: So the perimeter is 30.9 m to 1 d.p.

questions.question: Figure 3 shows a sign made of kite OABC joined to sector OCXA of a circle centre O. OA = OC = 0.6 m, AB = CB = 1.4 m, angle OAB = angle OCB = 2 radians, and angle AOC = theta radians. Show that theta = 1.64 radians to 3 significant figures.
steps: Cosine rule for angle AOB: cos(AOB) = (0.36 + 3.019 - 1.96) / (2 x 0.6 x 1.7376) = 0.6806.
The kite is symmetric about OB, so theta = angle AOC = 2 x 0.8222 = 1.644, so 1.64 to 3 s.f.

questions.question: Find the perimeter of the sign in metres to 2 significant figures.
steps: Perimeter = AB + BC + major arc AXC.

questions.question: Find the area of the sign in m^2 to 2 significant figures.
steps: So the area is 1.6 m^2 to 2 s.f.

questions.question: Figure 1 shows the plan of a garden. OA and CD are perpendicular to OD, AB is an arc of the circle with centre O and radius 4 m, BC is parallel to OD, OD = 6 m, OA = 4 m and CD = 1.5 m. Show that angle AOB is 1.186 radians to 4 significant figures.
steps: BC is parallel to OD and CD is perpendicular to OD, so B is 1.5 m above OD.
In triangle OBP (P the foot on OD): sin(BOD) = 1.5 / 4 = 0.375, so BOD = 0.3844 radians.
Angle AOB = pi/2 - BOD = 1.5708 - 0.3844 = 1.1864 radians, so 1.186 to 4 s.f.

questions.question: Find the perimeter of the garden in metres to 3 significant figures.
steps: Perimeter = OA + arc AB + BC + CD + DO.

questions.question: Find the area of the garden in square metres to 3 significant figures.
steps: OBCD is a trapezium with parallel sides BC = 2.2919 and OD = 6, height 1.5: (2.2919 + 6)/2 x 1.5 = 6.219 m^2.

questions.question: Figure 2 shows a semicircular garden with centre O, radius 3 m, diameter AOE. BD is parallel to AE and angle BOA = 0.7 radians. Show that angle BOD is 1.742 radians to 4 significant figures.
steps: B and D are symmetric about the perpendicular through O, so angle BOA = angle DOE = 0.7.
So angle BOD = 1.742 radians to 4 s.f.

questions.question: The flowerbed R is bounded by the chord BD and the arc BCD. Find the area of the flowerbed in square metres to 1 decimal place.
steps: Area of flowerbed = sector BOD - triangle BOD.

questions.question: Find the perimeter of the flowerbed in metres to 1 decimal place.
A sector AOB of a circle with centre O has radius r cm and angle theta radians. The area of the sector is 6 cm^2 and the perimeter is 10 cm. Show that 3theta^2 - 13theta + 12 = 0.
steps: Area: (1/2) r^2 theta = 6, so r^2 theta = 12.
Perimeter: 2r + r theta = 10, so r = 10/(2 + theta).
Substitute: 100 theta / (2 + theta)^2 = 12, so 100 theta = 12(4 + 4 theta + theta^2).
Expand and simplify: 12 theta^2 - 52 theta + 48 = 0, divide by 4: 3theta^2 - 13theta + 12 = 0.

questions.question: Hence find the possible values of r and theta for the sector in part (a).
steps: r = 10/(2 + theta): theta = 4/3 gives r = 3; theta = 3 gives r = 2.

questions.question: Figure 3 shows a roof support made of four beams AB, BD, BC and AD. AB = 6.5 m, BC = BD = 4.7 m and angle BAC = 35 degrees. Find the size of angle ACB to 1 decimal place.
steps: Sine rule in triangle ABC: sin(ACB) = AB sin(BAC) / BC = 6.5 sin(35) / 4.7 = 0.7932.
So ACB is 52.5 degrees or 127.5 degrees.
In the figure C lies between A and D with ACB obtuse, so ACB = 127.5 degrees.

questions.question: Using the structure in Figure 3, find the total length of wood needed to make the structure, to the nearest metre.
steps: A, C and D lie on one straight line, and BC = BD, so C and D are symmetric about the foot F of the perpendicular from B.
Total = AB + BD + BC + AD = 6.5 + 4.7 + 4.7 + 8.186 = 24.09 m, so 24 m to the nearest metre.

questions.question: Parallelogram ABCD has area 40 cm^2, AB = 10 cm, BC = 6 cm, and angle DAB is obtuse. Find the size of angle DAB in degrees to 2 decimal places.
steps: Area of parallelogram = AB x AD sin(DAB) with AD = BC = 6: 40 = 60 sin(DAB).
sin(DAB) = 2/3, so the acute angle is arcsin(2/3) = 41.81 degrees.
DAB is obtuse, so DAB = 180 - 41.81 = 138.19 degrees.

questions.question: Find the length of diagonal BD in cm to 1 decimal place.
steps: Cosine rule in triangle ABD: BD^2 = AB^2 + AD^2 - 2(AB)(AD) cos(DAB).

questions.question: In triangle ABC, AB = 21 cm, BC = 13 cm, angle BAC = 25 degrees and angle ACB = x degrees. Use the sine rule to find sin(x), giving your answer to 4 decimal places.
steps: Sine rule: AB / sin(ACB) = BC / sin(BAC).

questions.question: Given also that AB is the longest side of triangle ABC, find the value of x to 2 decimal places.
steps: From part (a), sin(x) = 0.6827, so x = 43.05 degrees or x = 136.95 degrees.
AB is the longest side, so angle ACB (opposite AB) is the largest angle.
Angle B = 180 - 25 - 43.05 = 111.95 would be bigger than C, so x = 43.05 is rejected.

questions.question: Shape ABCDA is a sector ABCOA of a circle with centre O and radius 6 cm, joined to triangle AOD, where D lies on OC, AD = 5 cm and angle AOD = 0.7 radians. Find the area of sector ABCOA to 1 d.p.
steps: The sector ABCOA is the major sector, so its angle is 2pi - 0.7 = 5.5832 radians.

questions.question: Given that angle ADO is obtuse, find the size of angle ADO in radians to 3 d.p.
steps: Sine rule: sin(ADO) / OA = sin(AOD) / AD, so sin(ADO) = 6 sin(0.7) / 5 = 0.7731.
ADO is obtuse, so ADO = pi - 0.8836 = 2.258 radians to 3 d.p.

questions.question: Hence find the perimeter of shape ABCDA to 1 d.p.
steps: Sine rule: OD = AD sin(OAD) / sin(AOD) = 5 x 0.1826 / 0.6442 = 1.417 cm, so CD = 6 - 1.417 = 4.583 cm.
Perimeter = arc ABC + CD + DA = 33.499 + 4.583 + 5 = 43.08, so 43.1 cm to 1 d.p.

questions.question: Figure 3 shows a viewing platform: sector ABCOA of a circle with centre O (OA = OC = 6 m) joined to triangle AOD, with AD = 14 m, angle ADC = 0.43 radians, angle AOD obtuse, and OCD a straight line. Find the size of angle AOD in radians to 3 d.p.
steps: Angle ADO = angle ADC = 0.43 radians, since C lies on OD.
Sine rule: sin(AOD) = AD sin(ADO) / OA = 14 sin(0.43) / 6 = 14 x 0.41687 / 6 = 0.97270.
AOD is obtuse, so AOD = pi - 1.3366 = 1.805 radians to 3 d.p.

questions.question: Find the length of arc ABC in metres to 1 d.p.
steps: Angle AOC = angle AOD = 1.805 radians, and arc ABC is the major arc on the other side.

questions.question: Find the total area of the viewing platform in m^2 to 1 d.p.
Curve C has equation y = f(x), where f(x) = (3x + 20)(x + 6)(2x - 3). Using the given information, state the values of x for which f(x) > 0.
steps: Roots of f(x) = 0 are x = -20/3, x = -6 and x = 3/2.
Leading coefficient is 3 x 1 x 2 = 6 > 0, so f(x) > 0 for x > 3/2.
The sign alternates between roots, so f(x) > 0 for -20/3 < x < -6.
So f(x) > 0 when -20/3 < x < -6 or x > 3/2.

questions.question: Expand (3x + 20)(x + 6)(2x - 3), writing the answer as a polynomial in simplest form.
Line l is the tangent to C at the point where C cuts the y-axis, and l cuts C again at point P. Using algebra, find the x coordinate of P. Calculator solutions are not acceptable.
steps: On the y-axis x = 0: f(0) = -360, so the point is (0, -360).
x = 0 is the repeated root (tangent point), so P has x = -67/6.

questions.question: The line l1 has equation 4y + 3x = 48 and cuts the y-axis at C. State the y coordinate of C.
Point D(8, 6) lies on l1. Line l2 passes through D and is perpendicular to l1, and cuts the y-axis at E. Show that the y coordinate of E is -14/3.
steps: Rewrite l1: y = -3x/4 + 12, so its gradient is -3/4.
Perpendicular gradient for l2 = 4/3. Line l2 through (8, 6): y - 6 = (4/3)(x - 8).

questions.question: A sector BCE of a circle with centre C has angle BCE = 1.8 radians. Find the length of arc BE.
steps: So the arc length BE is 30.

questions.question: The shaded region CBED consists of sector BCE joined to triangle CDE. Calculate the exact area of region CBED.
steps: Triangle CDE has base CE = 50/3 on the y-axis and height equal to the x coordinate of D, which is 8.

questions.question: Figure 2 shows a house ABCD (rectangle, AB = 16 m) and lawn APCDA. APCOA is a sector of a circle with centre O and radius 12 m, and O lies on the line DC. Show that angle AOD is 1.231 radians to 3 decimal places.
steps: DC = AB = 16 m and OC = 12 m (radius), so DO = 16 - 12 = 4 m.
In the right-angled triangle AOD (right angle at D), cos(AOD) = DO / OA = 4/12 = 1/3.

questions.question: The lawn APCDA is shaded in Figure 2. Find the area of the lawn in m^2 to 1 decimal place.
steps: Angle AOC (through the bottom of the sector) = 2pi - (pi - 1.231) = pi + 1.231 = 4.3726 radians.
The house part of the sector is triangle AOD, with area (1/2)(DO)(AD) = (1/2)(4)(sqrt(144 - 16)) = 22.63 m^2.

questions.question: Find the perimeter of the lawn APCDA in metres to 1 decimal place.
steps: Perimeter = major arc APC + CD + DA.

questions.question: Figure 2 shows a pond design: sector AOBX of a circle with centre O (OA = OB = 3 m) joined to quadrilateral AOBC, with angle AOB = 2pi/3 radians, BC = 8 m and angle BCA = pi/6 radians. Calculate (i) the exact area of sector AOBX, and (ii) the exact perimeter of sector AOBX.
steps: Sector AOBX is the major sector through X, with angle 2pi - 2pi/3 = 4pi/3.
(ii) Arc length = 3 x 4pi/3 = 4pi m, and two radii add 3 + 3 = 6 m.

questions.question: Calculate the exact area of triangle AOB in the pond design.
Show that the length AB is 3sqrt(3) m.
steps: Cosine rule in triangle AOB: AB^2 = OA^2 + OB^2 - 2(OA)(OB) cos(2pi/3).

questions.question: Find the total surface area of the pond in m^2 correct to 2 significant figures.
steps: Pond = sector AOBX + triangle AOB + triangle ABC.
Sector = 6pi = 18.85 m^2 and triangle AOB = 9sqrt(3)/4 = 3.897 m^2.
Triangle ABC: area = (1/2)(BC)(AC) sin(30 degrees) with AC from cosine rule: 27 = AC^2 + 64 - 8sqrt(3) AC, giving AC = 4sqrt(3) + sqrt(11) = 10.245 m (the valid root for this layout).

questions.question: Circle C has centre O, P and S are points on C, and OPQRSO is a sector with arc PS of length 0.72 m and angle POS = 0.6 radians. Show that OP = 1.2 m.
steps: Arc PS = r theta, so 0.72 = OP x 0.6.

questions.question: The target area PQRS (sector OQRSO minus sector OPS) is 90 m^2 and PQ = x m. Show that 5x^2 + 12x - 1500 = 0.
steps: Outer radius OQ = 1.2 + x; inner radius OP = 1.2; angle 0.6 radians.

questions.question: Hence calculate the total perimeter of the target area PQRS to the nearest metre.
steps: Outer radius OQ = 1.2 + 16.16 = 17.36 m, so arc QR = 0.6 x 17.36 = 10.42 m.
Perimeter = PQ + arc QR + RS + arc SP = 16.16 + 10.42 + 16.16 + 0.72 = 43.46 m.
So the perimeter is 43 m to the nearest metre.

questions.question: Figure 2 shows a plan of a frame for a flat roof: triangle ABD joined to triangle BCD, with BD = x m, CD = (1 + x) m, BC = 5 m, angle BCD = theta degrees, and ADC a straight line. Show that cos(theta) = (13 + x)/(5 + 5x).
steps: Cosine rule in triangle BCD: BD^2 = BC^2 + CD^2 - 2(BC)(CD) cos(theta).

questions.question: Given also that x = 2sqrt(3), angle BAC = 30 degrees and ADC is a straight line, find the area of triangle ABC in m^2 to 1 d.p.
steps: cos(theta) = (13 + 2sqrt(3)) / (5 + 10sqrt(3)) = 0.7376, so sin(theta) = 0.6752 and theta = 42.5 degrees.
Angle ACB = theta (since A, D, C are collinear), so angle ABC = 180 - 30 - 42.5 = 107.5 degrees.
Sine rule in triangle ABC: AC = BC sin(ABC) / sin(BAC) = 5 sin(107.5) / 0.5 = 5 x 0.9536 / 0.5 = 9.536 m.
